notes: Dev RBox contraction paired with technology-replace-d006: it removes the property the revision changes, the symmetry of is_directly_connected_to. The earlier version of this record removed the inverse of written_in, a near paraphrase that a model answers from word meaning; symmetry of a link is not a paraphrase of itself. The two instance questions use the revision's scenes (laptop and router, desktop and printer) but without the cable: a named cable joins two devices at both ends whatever happens to the abstract axiom, so 'yes' would have a route back through world knowledge; they are asked as plain converse questions ('Is the router directly connected to the laptop?') so that 'I don't know' is the one fair answer once the property is gone, not 'No, it does not follow'. They therefore differ in wording from the revision's prompts, which keep the cable. Both original answers are 'yes' and become 'I don't know'. The cross-lingual queries ask the first instance. hops counts the instance premise in the prompt as the bridge (1 + 1), the convention of the geography RBox template (the README table lists RBox derived as 1 hop; the records follow the template and the revision). Near unrelated: the same property of another networking relation (is on the same local network as, symmetric), which an over-applied removal would blank; far unrelated: a different property of an unrelated relation. The instance premises are claimed definitional: generic scenes, not stored facts. The infini-gram API answered on 2026-11-12 but there is nothing to count for generic scenes; the Wi-Fi side facts rest on the Wikipedia note of the paired revision.
